title: Assessing Soft Error Reliability in Vectorized Kernels: Vulnerability and Performance Trade-Offs on Arm and RISC-V ISAs
problem: Vector extensions (Arm SVE, RISC-V RVV) on high-performance processors increase vulnerability to soft errors. The relationship between register cross-section, vector operations, and soft error criticality is not well characterized.
motivation: Radiation-resilient computing is critical as high-performance processors with vector extensions are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications. Understanding soft error vulnerability is essential for reliability trade-off analysis.
method: Uniform random fault injection techniques assess soft error vulnerability in vectorized kernels on Arm and RISC-V ISAs. The study correlates soft error criticality to register cross-section and vectorized benchmark characteristics.
key_novelty: Systematic characterization of soft error vulnerability in modern vector ISAs (Arm SVE, RISC-V RVV) and their correlation to register cross-section and workload characteristics.
contributions: Quantified soft error criticality correlation to register cross-section
Performance and reliability trade-off analysis for vector extensions
Uniform fault injection methodology for vectorized kernels
primary_theme: Soft error assessment in vector ISA kernels
